mission_2.prediction: I chose BFS and DFS. I predict BFS will finish sooner on the constrained map. In Mission 1, BFS found the shortest 24.5 m route, while my DFS route was 50.0 m because the stack follows one branch deeply and keeps the first route it finds. Both robots share the same 0.30 m/s speed, so the DFS robot has twice the distance to drive. The DFS route probably contains more turns and zig-zags, where the controller slows down, which means it can take longer.
mission_2.performance:
Constrained map, BFS vs DFS:
- BFS: succeeded, elapsed_s 90.6 s, distance_m 23.9 m (planned 24.5 m), goal error 0.26 m.
- DFS: controller_failed, elapsed_s 146.1 s, distance_m 31.8 m of a 50.0 m planned route, ending 5.88 m from the goal.

The result supported my prediction. BFS reached the goal, and DFS never did. DFS had already driven farther and longer than the whole BFS journey when it stopped.

The DFS route fills the middle room with about six zigzags, because the stack keeps following one branch, and the first branch to reach the goal snakes back and forth. The controller slows for every hairpin turn, so DFS averaged only about 0.22 m/s. My retained checkpoint (sample 1462, t = 148.6 s, x = 1.10, y = -2.31) is where it stopped: speed 0.00 m/s, right at the turn around the bottom of the central wall, where the route hugs the wall. Tracking error there was only 0.02 m, so this was not the robot drifting off the path. So the DFS route quality, its length, and the tight wall-hugging turns caused both the extra time and the failure.
mission_2.choice:
I would choose Nav2 Smac 2D for delivery. It succeeded on both maps: 35.8 s on the open map and 73.3 s on the constrained map, which was the fastest or near-fastest on each.

Compared with my A*.  A* also succeeded on both maps but needed 46.4 s (open) and 90.2 s (constrained), because its 4-connected grid route is a staircase. Nav2 drove 10.1 m vs 13.2 m on the open map and 20.5 m vs 23.9 m on the constrained map. A* tracked its path slightly more closely on the open map (mean tracking error 0.016 m vs 0.042 m), but both are a few centimetres, far below the 0.25 m goal tolerance. On the constrained map, Nav2 kept more estimated wall clearance (0.27 m vs 0.12 m) because it is cost-aware.

Nav2 is deterministic. The advantage that matters most for delivery is reaching the goal reliably in the shortest time while staying away from walls, which Smac created a smoothed, cost-aware route, keeping the robot moving faster when it needs to turn.
